findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut and can throw on short prefixes
findings.body: The new matcher has three defects. (1) The slice `substring(3, 5)` is wrong: in a token ID like `onrtac:<uuid>` the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 (`substring(4, 6)`), so `substring(3, 5)` yields `ta` and never equals a real grant shortcut. (2) The condition is inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the token exactly when the grant matches. (3) `items[0]` is not length-checked, so a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the matcher. As written, the four new grant-specific assertions (CODE_TO_TOKEN, DEVICE_CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN, AUTHREQID_TO_TOKEN) only verify the UUID suffix and never the grant. Fixing only the offset would make the matcher reject correct tokens, so the logic must be fixed together with the offset.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
findings.body: The second `Objects.requireNonNull` call tests `grantType` again (copy-paste error) and its message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. The `rawTokenId` parameter is therefore never validated. A null raw ID would be accepted and `encodeTokenId` would produce a token ID ending in `:null`, which is then written into the access token `jti` claim and event details. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
findings.body: The test sets up the factory with `init()` only and never calls `postInit()`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For the unknown grant shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls through to `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory and throws NullPointerException. The test catches any RuntimeException, so it passes even if the decoder's 'Unknown value ... for grant type' IllegalArgumentException path were broken or removed. The test should set up a session factory stub (or assert the specific IllegalArgumentException type and message) so it verifies the intended behaviour.

findings.title: Shortcut doc says 3 letters, but the encoder hard-codes 2-character slots and nothing validates it
findings.body: The Javadoc suggests 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires exactly 6 characters for the context (2 per slot) and encodeTokenId concatenates the shortcut as-is. A grant factory that follows this doc and returns a 3-character shortcut will get tokens minted with a 7-character prefix that the decoder rejects ('Expected length of 6'). Also, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit passes `getShortcut()` straight into a ConcurrentHashMap, so a null return causes a NullPointerException and fails server startup with no clear message. postInit should validate that each shortcut is non-null and exactly 2 characters, and the Javadoc should state that requirement.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Every existing implementation of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside the bundled grants (custom or downstream grant types) will fail to compile, and if the method is not implemented it will fail at runtime during postInit. A default implementation, or a documented migration note, would avoid breaking third-party SPI implementors.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed without replacement
findings.body: The diff deletes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context. This is an unexplained removal from a public SPI type. Any caller in the codebase or downstream that copies a context will no longer compile. The description does not mention the removal, and the new `grantType` field is not carried over by any copy path. If the removal is intentional it should be called out, or the constructor should be kept (and updated to copy `grantType`).

findings.title: Access token jti is no longer a UUID; this externally visible change is undocumented
findings.body: The access token `jti` claim, and the `TOKEN_ID` value written to event details, change from a plain UUID to `<6 chars>:<uuid>`. RFC 7519 allows this, but clients and log/analytics pipelines that parse `jti` as a UUID (for example into a UUID-typed column) will break. The PR does not mention this in its description, release notes, or any migration guidance. This should be documented as a visible behaviour change, and existing consumers should be checked.

findings.title: Production encoding path (getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext) has no test coverage
findings.body: The only unit tests exercise decode/encode round-trips from a hand-written string. Nothing tests `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, which is the code that actually runs in TokenManager.initToken for every access token. It has no coverage for the TRANSIENT vs ONLINE vs OFFLINE session-type selection, the lightweight vs regular token-type selection, or the fallback to 'na' when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is absent. Combined with the broken AssertEvents matcher, no test verifies the token ID that is actually issued. Tests for these cases should be added.
